Orthokeratology (OrthoK) lenses are specially designed contact lenses worn overnight. They gently reshape the cornea while sleeping, allowing clear vision during the day without glasses or contact lenses.
We find that families find this particularly useful when their children are playing sports. There are families that prefer their kids to not wear glasses and they find this useful too.
In children, OrthoK lenses are also used as part of myopia management to help slow progression in selected cases. Proper evaluation, precise fitting, and regular follow-up are essential to ensure safety and effectiveness.

Doctors recommend OrthoK after assessing eye measurements, corneal health, and suitability for the child’s age and lifestyle.

Book an appointment to evaluate OrthoK suitability.

Myopia (short-sightedness) often begins in childhood and may increase as a child grows. Lately, we have been seeing this growth continue upto even 18-19 years of age which is a concern. The Myopia Control Clinic at Eye Solutions focuses on early assessment, monitoring progression, and offering evidence-based strategies to help manage myopia.

Each child undergoes a detailed vision and eye health evaluation, followed by personalised guidance based on age, eye measurements, and lifestyle factors. Management plans are designed to support long-term visual health while fitting into a child’s daily routine.

Early evaluation allows parents to understand progression patterns and available options clearly.

Book an appointment at the Myopia Control Clinic.

Squint occurs when the eyes do not align properly, causing each eye to focus in a different direction. In children, this can interfere with normal visual development and may lead to reduced vision in one eye if not monitored early. Some children may not complain of vision problems, making regular eye checks important.

In adults, squint can cause eye strain, headaches, double vision, or difficulty with depth perception. It may develop gradually or appear suddenly due to changes in vision, nerve function, or muscle balance.

Squint is not always constant and may appear only during fatigue, illness, or prolonged screen use. Early assessment helps identify whether the squint is intermittent or persistent and whether it affects visual function.

An eye examination allows doctors to evaluate eye alignment, vision, and binocular function and advise on observation, correction, or treatment when needed.

Book an eye check-up for squint assessment.

Squint (misalignment of the eyes) can affect vision, depth perception, and eye comfort in both children and adults. At Eye Solutions, squint management begins with a detailed evaluation to understand the type, cause, and impact on vision.

Treatment may involve glasses, exercises, or surgical correction, depending on individual findings. Squint surgery aims to improve eye alignment and visual coordination through a planned and measured approach.

Early evaluation helps determine the most appropriate course of care and timing of treatment.

Book an appointment for a squint evaluation.

Cataracts develop slowly and often go unnoticed in the early stages. Many people assume their changing vision is simply a part of ageing, but recognising early signs can help with timely evaluation and planning.

Common early symptoms include blurred or hazy vision, increased glare from lights, difficulty driving at night, faded colours, and frequent changes in spectacle power. Some people also notice that reading becomes harder even with updated glasses.

Cataracts are not an emergency condition, but regular eye check-ups are important to monitor progression. Early assessment allows your doctor to explain the condition, discuss lifestyle impact, and advise on the right time for treatment - if and when needed.

If you are experiencing persistent visual changes or feel your vision is not as sharp as before, an eye examination can help clarify the cause and guide you appropriately.

Book an eye check-up to understand your vision better

Exposure to smoke, pollution, chemical fumes, and gas leaks can irritate the eyes and affect daily comfort. 

Common symptoms include:

• Redness
• Burning sensation
• Itching
• Watering eyes
• Dryness
• Blurred vision

These irritants can disrupt the eye's natural tear film, leading to discomfort and increased sensitivity. People with dry eyes, allergies, or contact lenses may be more vulnerable.

To protect your eyes:

• Use lubricating eye drops if recommended
• Improve indoor ventilation
• Avoid smoke and chemical exposure
• Wear protective eyewear in high-risk environments
• Avoid rubbing irritated eyes

If symptoms persist, worsen, or affect your vision, seek professional eye care promptly.

Dry eye is one of the most common ocular surface problems today, affecting 32% of Indians (AIOS data, 2023). When the tear film becomes unstable, the cornea—the clear front window of the eye—starts to dry out, leading to burning, redness, fluctuating vision, and light sensitivity. Dr Kavita Rao, leading cornea specialist in Bandra–Khar, explains that untreated dry eye can gradually cause corneal surface damage, tiny epithelial defects, and increased risk of infections.

Screen overuse, air‑conditioned environments, ageing, hormonal changes, and certain medications worsen symptoms. Many patients assume it is “normal tiredness,” but persistent dryness needs evaluation. Treatment ranges from lubricating drops and warm compresses to advanced options like punctal plugs or serum drops, depending on severity.

Protecting the cornea early prevents long‑term complications. If you experience gritty sensation, blurred vision that improves after blinking, or discomfort by evening, get your eyes examined promptly.

Wearing sunglasses outdoors helps protect your eyes from bright light and UV rays. Common side effects include mild irritation, redness, and sensitivity to light, but these usually subside quickly.

Healthy corneas depend on small, consistent habits. In India’s dusty, sunny climate, these habits matter even more.
Dr Kavita Rao explains that the cornea stays healthy when it’s protected from dryness, UV rays, and infections.

Daily habits that help:
· Avoid rubbing your eyes
· Keep contact lenses clean and replace them on time
· Wear UVprotected sunglasses
· Stay hydrated
· Follow the 202020 rule for screen use
· Maintain clean hands and makeup hygiene

These simple steps reduce the risk of infections, abrasions, and longterm corneal damage.

A mild red eye after long screen hours may be harmless. But a red eye with severe pain, sudden vision drop, white spots on the cornea, or intense light sensitivity can indicate a corneal emergency.

Corneal ulcers are especially common in India due to dust, trauma, and improper contact lens hygiene (AIOS).
Dr Kavita Rao stresses that corneal ulcers can progress within hours, making early treatment essential.

Seek urgent care if you notice:
· Severe redness
· Sharp pain
· Blurred vision
· Discharge
· A white/grey spot on the cornea
Prompt treatment prevents scarring and vision loss.

Cataract surgery is a minimally invasive procedure, and most patients have a quick recovery. Dr Kavita Rao, ophthalmologist in Khar, informs that some patients notice improvement in their vision within 24-48 hours, but complete healing typically takes four to six weeks.

During the initial days, mild discomfort, redness, and blurred vision are common, but these gradually subside. Patients are usually advised to avoid strenuous activities, heavy lifting, and rubbing their eyes for at least a week. Driving should be resumed only after confirming with your eye surgeon.
Most people can return to light activities within a few days, but full recovery varies depending on individual health conditions.

Following post-operative instructions, using prescribed eye drops, and visiting your eye doctor for follow-ups help ensure a smooth recovery. If any complications such as severe pain, swelling, or vision loss occur, consult your eye surgeon immediately.

Healthy Vision Month is the perfect time to focus on protecting your eyesight through simple, everyday practices. Dr. Kavita Rao, Ophthalmologist at PD Hinduja Hospital, Mumbai, emphasizes that maintaining eye health is not only about treating conditions—it’s about prevention and lifestyle.

Key steps for healthy vision include:
● Following the 20‑20‑20 rule to ease digital eye strain
● Wearing UV‑protective sunglasses outdoors
● Eating a diet rich in leafy greens, fish, and vitamins that support eye health
● Scheduling regular eye exams to detect issues early
● Encouraging children to get routine vision screenings for better learning outcomes

Ignoring eye health can lead to problems like glaucoma, diabetic eye disease, or severe dryness that affect daily life. Preventive care and timely attention help preserve clear vision for years to come.
This Healthy Vision Month, commit to small changes that make a big difference. With expert guidance from Dr. Kavita Rao at PD Hinduja Hospital, Mumbai, you can enjoy strong, healthy eyes at every stage of life.

Red eyes are common, but not all redness is harmless. In India’s hot, dusty climate, corneal infections and allergies are frequent.

Dr Kavita Rao explains that redness linked to corneal disease often comes with pain, blurred vision, discharge, or light sensitivity — signs that the cornea may be inflamed or infected.

Possible corneal causes of redness:
· Keratitis (infection)
· Dry eye disease
· Allergic eye disease
· Corneal abrasion
· Contact lens complications

Selfmedicating with steroid drops can worsen infections. A proper eye exam helps identify the cause and prevent complications.
